correctness.rationale: An exact, inductively correct bitset recurrence encodes exactly j distinct positive divisors, with descending-cardinality update preventing reuse. Whole range 0..n! enumerated for each n <= 12; at n=12 the 792 genuine divisors cover 479001601 sums at cardinality <=8 but leave exactly 175 positive targets uncovered at <=7. The complete list of 175 target integers is recomputed and compared byte-independent of its source data. The same argument determines h(1!), ..., h(11!). C++ uses a separate word-array representation for n=8..11. These are finite calculations supported by a proof of exhaustiveness; nothing is asserted for n>=13.

value.rationale: The natural extremal invariant h(n!) appears explicitly in Erdős Problem 18 and recent work. The first exact 8-term threshold is a meaningful finite classification of its initial growth, accompanied by a complete exceptional set of only 175 out of 479001600 positive targets and oddness/upper-tail structure. This resolves a complete concrete finite boundary, not an arbitrary modular restriction. The dataset and exact replay provide useful small-n benchmarks; no downstream/asymptotic theorem is invented or required.
